title: Spec
description: A spec: one coherent capability the system must provide — a product behavior, or a technical implementation needed to support the product's rules — with its specifics captured as acceptance criteria. Most are extracted from the PRD; some capture supporting technical capabilities.

title.description: One-line capability description. Imperative, directive, no filler

description.description: Short, concrete summary of the capability: the problem it solves and who or what is affected. General only — leave the specifics to acceptance_criteria and the step-by-step implementation to plan.md.

acceptance_criteria.description: Verifiable acceptance criteria, each with a stable id and its commitment level as a key (`must`, `must_not`, `should`, `should_not`, or `may`) holding the criterion text. Order by commitment level: must, then must_not, then should, then should_not, then may. `spex coverage` requires every criterion of an active or in-progress spec to have its own impl and test annotation (`@spec impl|test <spec-id>#<ac-id>`), and counts a criterion as done once its impl annotation is present — a missing test annotation is reported separately, as a gap or as pending.

items.description: A single verifiable acceptance criterion, exactly one of `must`/`must_not`/`should`/`should_not`/`may` present.

must.description: The criterion text for a mandatory requirement.

must_not.description: The criterion text for a prohibition.

should.description: The criterion text for a recommendation.

should_not.description: The criterion text for a discouraged behavior.

may.description: The criterion text for an optional behavior.

is_done.description: Whether this criterion is actually done. Optional; omitting it counts as true. `spex-spec` sets it false on every criterion of a newly authored spec; `spex-test` clears it (removes the field) once `spex coverage` shows the criterion fully impl+test traced. `spex check` requires every criterion true (or absent) before a spec's status can be active.

packages.description: Package short names targeted for implementing this spec. Each must match a package_short_name in spex.yaml.

blocked_by.description: Spec IDs that must be in place before this spec can be implemented. List only genuine blockers that are not yet satisfied; remove one once it ships or is established. Absent or empty means nothing blocks this spec. Do not list a shared foundation that every capability rides on (e.g. the API surface) — only the specs whose absence prevents this one from being built.

items.description: A spec ID that blocks this spec: this spec cannot be implemented until that spec is in place.

status.description: Lifecycle status. Omitting is equivalent to 'planned'. 'active' means fully implemented and requires every acceptance criterion to be done (`is_done` absent or true), enforced by `spex check`; use 'in-progress' while any criterion is still `is_done: false`. Whether those criteria are actually traced by annotations is `spex coverage`'s job.

contract.description: Contract coverage granularity, required. `none` disables contract coverage entirely; `single` requires a single `@spec contract <spec-id>` annotation for the whole spec; `for-each-ac` requires a `@spec contract <spec-id>#<ac-id>` annotation for every acceptance criterion.

coverage_ignore.description: Coverage requirements to waive. Each entry is `{layer, ac}`: `layer` (`contract`, `impl`, or `test`) is required; `ac` is optional — omit it to waive that layer for the whole spec (every acceptance criterion, for impl/test), or give an acceptance criterion id to waive just that one criterion's impl or test annotation, or its contract annotation under `contract: for-each-ac`. `spex check` verifies each entry matches the spec's `contract` setting.

examples.description: Named illustrative snippets showing the spec applied in context — placement and usage that prose cannot carry. Keys are short labels (e.g. `template`, `contract`, `avoid`, `prefer`); values are code or text blocks.

examples.title: Allow customers to place an order from their cart
examples.description: Lets authenticated shoppers turn their cart into a paid order.

acceptance_criteria.must: create an order only when the cart contains at least one item
capture payment before the order is marked as confirmed
empty the customer's cart after the order is successfully placed

acceptance_criteria.should: display an order confirmation with a unique order number
